title: Surcharge rules

act2.summary: a hazmat surcharge arrives that only applies when two existing surcharges (remote-area and oversize) already do - a rule about the relationship between surcharges, not a new independent one

solutions.title: One class per surcharge, computed from the shipment alone
solutions.tradeoff: The most expensive of all four measured routes. The shared id union has to grow, a new class carries the usual per-strategy boilerplate for one check, and - because no strategy can see another strategy's result - it still has to re-derive 'is remote and is oversize' from the raw shipment instead of reading remoteArea/oversize's already-computed amounts.

solutions.title: A Record of named surcharge functions, each pure in the shipment
solutions.tradeoff: Cheaper than Strategy - no class ceremony, just one more key and function - but the same isolation problem: each entry is a pure function of the shipment alone, so the new entry still has to re-derive the cross-condition rather than read it. Ties the no-pattern baseline on hunks but costs more lines and touches one more file.

solutions.title: An ordered list of rules, each seeing every surcharge computed before it
solutions.tradeoff: The only candidate that reads rather than re-derives: the new rule checks the accumulator's already-computed remoteArea and oversize amounts directly. Fewest lines of any of the four measured routes, including the no-pattern baseline - but one more hunk than the baseline, because the change lands in three separate spots (the id union, the rules array, the return literal) instead of inside two self-contained function bodies the baseline already had.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
Is 'a rule about the relationship between surcharges, not a new independent one' a fair reading of why this act 2 sits outside Strategy's usual strength?
In the strategy and lookup-table routes, does the hazmat check really re-derive 'is remote and is oversize' from the raw shipment, rather than reading the other surcharges' already-computed amounts?
Does the no-pattern baseline actually beat every structured candidate on hunks, and is that reported honestly rather than picked around?
Would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have predicted that none of the three candidates - not even the winner - beats the no-pattern baseline on every dimension?
